cards.front: Recall a key point about Family Law
cards.back: Marriage in England and Wales is governed by the Marriage Act 1949 — it must be monogamous, between two people over 16 (with parental consent under 18)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Family Law
cards.back: A valid marriage requires: both parties must freely consent, they must not be within prohibited degrees of relationship, and the marriage must be properly solemnised

cards.front: Recall a key point about Family Law
cards.back: Civil partnerships were introduced in 2004 for same-sex couples and extended to opposite-sex couples in 2019 — they provide similar legal rights to marriage

cards.front: Recall a key point about Family Law
cards.back: Divorce is governed by the Matrimonial Causes Act 1973 — since April 2022, no-fault divorce allows either party to apply without proving fault

cards.front: Recall a key point about Family Law
cards.back: Under no-fault divorce, a spouse simply states the marriage has broken down irretrievably — there is a 20-week reflection period before the conditional decree

cards.front: Recall a key point about Family Law
cards.back: The court decides financial arrangements on divorce using factors under section 25 of the Matrimonial Causes Act 1973 — including needs, income, duration and contributions

cards.front: Recall a key point about Family Law
cards.back: The Children Act 1989 makes the child's welfare the paramount consideration in all decisions about their upbringing

cards.front: Recall a key point about Family Law
cards.back: Parental responsibility is the legal rights and duties of a parent — mothers always have it; married fathers have it automatically; unmarried fathers can acquire it

cards.front: Recall a key point about Family Law
cards.back: CAFCASS (Children and Family Court Advisory and Support Service) represents children's interests in family court proceedings

cards.front: Recall a key point about Family Law
cards.back: Child protection measures include care orders, supervision orders and emergency protection orders where a child is at risk of significant harm

cards.front: Recall a key point about Family Law
cards.back: The Domestic Abuse Act 2021 recognises economic abuse and controlling behaviour as forms of domestic abuse, not just physical violence

cards.front: Recall a key point about Family Law
cards.back: Family courts are private (not open to the public) to protect the privacy of children and families

cards.front: What should you know about gcse law exam tips — family law?
cards.back: 1. For Family Law questions, identify the relevant area of law and state the legal principles clearly 2. Apply legal rules to the facts of the scenario — don't just state the law 3. When evaluating, consider both the effectiveness and fairness of legal rules 4. Reference relevant cases and statutes when discussing Family Law 5. Consider reform proposals and alternative approaches where relevant
How effectively does family law protect the interests of children? (15 marks)

AO1 (Knowledge & Understanding): Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of family law, including key legal rules, principles and concepts relevant to OCR J271. AO2 (Application): Apply knowledge and understanding of family law to legal scenarios and problems, using legal reasoning and analysis. AO3 (Analysis & Evaluation): Analyse, evaluate and critique legal rules, principles and reform proposal
